reviews.comment: Polsley made the class really enjoyable. He actually knows what it's like to be a student and is forgiving. You won't have busywork. Definitely take him if you can.

It was honestly a joy to have Polsley as a professor. His lectures were clear and accessible. He implemented one of the clearest and most fair grading systems I have ever seen and the programming assignments were not too difficult (but you still learned a lot from doing them). He is truly knowledgeable and I would recommend taking him!

I never give RMP ratings but had to give Polsley a 5. He is by far the most caring and helpful professor I've had so far. He is always willing to help students out with homework or programming assignments and I can recall multiples occasions of him staying past his office hours to help students out.

Professor Polsley is one of the most enthusiastic and kind professors you will ever meet. One thing I loved most about his class is that the workload was not overwhelming. The assignments and lectures helped us understand the various data structures and taught us some essential skills to have in computer programming (such as debugging).

I do not normally rate professors, but I had to rate Prof. Polsley. 

Professor Polsley is an incredible professor and beyond kind and passionate about what he does, it really shows. He structures content and PAs about topics that students are genuinely interested in and is super helpful and accessible. If you have the chance, take his class.

Polsley is an amazing Professor. He is very caring and really wants the students to learn. The labs are a bit tough but you can work with others. The PAs are definitely time-consuming so please allow enough time to complete the PAs. Exams are a little touch but you should be good as long as you study. There are also quizzes and hws. Keep up w/ pace

The GOAT! Seth is a real one. He cares about all his students and is willing to spend lots of time after class in-office hours helping his students with whatever conceptual or homework questions. Easily one of my favorite professors at A&M. Very kind and encouraging. Cannot understate how goated this man.

Had him for 121, so when I saw that he taught 221, I had to take him!! Extremely nice prof, great lecture style, best grading scale (projects ~40%, exams are ~35% together), and really cares about your learning of skills and concepts for future endeavors i.e. CS industry jobs. Very passionate about CS & will do more for his students than most.

When I say he's amazing, he's amazing. Incredibly nice professor and I don't even need to take the others to tell that he's the best. Don't listen to a single negative review, the work/tests are straightforward and he is understanding. Please take my advice and choose him as your professor, trust me, you won't regret it. TRUST ME.

This is a defense for Seth b/c he's a real gem of a professor! I think even 1 rating was for CSCE222, which he doesn't even teach (only 121 so far)!! Don't listen to those bad ratings, anyone who's had him will tell you that they love his class. He's very polite & understands students' concerns with the material and grades! He's a cool guy overall

This is a difficult class no doubt (class is structured so that all sections with all profs are together), but regardless he was sensitive to our situations during the pandemic and always helped us to perform our best! He always answered our questions, and cared about how we were doing. Under the given circumstances, he was the best prof I had.

He is the first Computer Science teacher that I learned actual coding from, much better than any of my CS teachers in high school. If you have learned any programming basics in python or java, you will do fine. You can join his office hours and he will help with anything-labs, homework, concepts learned in class, and computer history facts :D.
reviews.ratingTags: Accessible outside class--Clear grading criteria--EXTRA CREDIT

reviews.comment: He isn't exactly the most helpful guy nor is he that great at what he does. I'm surprised he is allowed to attempt to teach since his justifications for many class related content are quite poor and have no actual logical backing to them. I wouldn't recommend him.
reviews.ratingTags: Lots of homework--Get ready to read--Tough grader

reviews.comment: I don't even have him as my professor, but I like him a lot! (spring 2021 is an online-semester, so for csce121 class, we have access to other prof's lectures). Lecture is very clear, and easy to follow. Always gives lots of example to make sure students understand the concept. If you're a curious person and like learning , definitely take him!

Very clear in lectures, goes through the basics to help students understand what their code is actually doing. One time I went to office hours and couldn't figure out what was wrong and had to leave, but he emailed me after working on it himself with the solution! Definitely wants to help us learn how to program
